Miriam Grijota Chousa is a statistician, data manager, and biostatistician who plays a key role in the clinical quality development and data management of cardiovascular healthcare in Denmark. She is heavily involved in the administration and analysis of data for the [[databasen-for-atrieflimren-i-danmark|Databasen for Atrieflimren i Danmark]] (AFDK), contributing to the evidence base used for political and clinical decision-making regarding atrial fibrillation treatment [^src1]. 

Her professional affiliations and governance roles have been documented across multiple annual reporting periods. In the 2023 AFDK annual report, she is identified as a biostatistician working for the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP) and is listed as a member of the database's governing body [^src1]. By the 2024 report, she continues her role as a biostatistician for RKKP and is explicitly noted as a member of the [[afdk-styregruppe|Styregruppen for AFDK]] (AFDK Steering Committee), reflecting her ongoing involvement in the interdisciplinary and cross-sectoral governance of the quality development program [^src2]. In the most recent 2025 documentation, her affiliation is listed with [[sundhedsvaesenets-kvalitetsinstitut|Sundhedsvæsenets Kvalitetsinstitut]] (SundK), indicating a transition or alignment with the Danish Healthcare Quality Institute while maintaining her core title as a statistician and data manager [^src3]. 

Through these roles, Chousa's work supports the broader Danish healthcare quality infrastructure. Her statistical and data management expertise ensures that critical information regarding incident and prevalent populations, mortality, and clinical outcomes—such as ischemic stroke incidence and anticoagulation wait times—are rigorously maintained and analyzed at both national and regional levels [^src1][^src3].
